title: She Woke Up Under a Seat in the Jungle: The Full Case of Annette Herfkens
description:
Case 023, the full case file. Annette Herfkens, a Dutch trader at a bank in Madrid, flew to Vietnam in November 1992 to see her fiancé of thirteen years, Willem van der Pas, whom she called Pasje. He had planned a few days by the sea in Nha Trang. She was claustrophobic and did not want to board the small jet; he told her the flight was only twenty minutes. Well into the flight, on 14 November 1992, Vietnam Airlines Flight 474, a Yakovlev Yak-40, dropped twice in bad weather, came down too low and hit the trees on a mountain ridge. Thirty of the 31 people aboard died. She had not been wearing a seat belt and woke with a seat on top of her, her jaw broken, a lung collapsed and her hip shattered. Willem had died in his seat. One other passenger, a Vietnamese businessman, was alive; he gave her a pair of trousers from his suitcase and told her rescuers would come, and then he died too. She decided to stay put, refused to let herself think about Willem, and worked out how to drink: she dragged herself on her elbows to the broken wing, pulled out its insulation, rolled it into balls and let the rain soak them, allowing herself a sip every two hours. For eight days rainwater was all she had. Nobody found the wreck. She has said she stayed in the moment and found calm in the beauty of the jungle, and that when she felt herself slipping away it felt beautiful. A man in orange appeared and went away again. On the eighth day men climbed up with body bags and a passenger list, among them a police officer who, she has said, took her for a ghost; she pointed to her own name. They carried her down in a sling of canvas, and she was taken to hospital in Singapore. At home her family already believed she was dead and death notices had been published; a colleague, Jaime Lupa, had refused to believe it. In December 1992 she attended Willem's funeral in Breda on a stretcher. By New Year's Eve she was walking and by February 1993 she was back at work. She later married Jaime Lupa, moved to New York and raised two children, went back to the mountain in 2006, and wrote a memoir, Turbulence.

Animated reconstruction of a true story. Every place and person is a generic low-poly reconstruction: no likeness is attempted, the aircraft is a generic three-engine jet, and the trading floor, the office in Vietnam, the airport, the hospital room, the funeral hall, the park and the skyline are not models of the real ones. Staging details (where people stood, what they wore, the suitcase, the clipboard, the fireworks in the window, the park walk, the writing desk and everything Rook does) are reconstruction, not record. Sources disagree on some details (24 or 25 passengers; how far into the flight the plane dropped; how soon the other survivor died; which day the man in orange came; seven or eight killed in the helicopter crash), so the narration says only what they agree on. Narration is a synthetic voice (Kokoro).

experiments.spine: v2 for long-form: cold open on the crash and her waking under the seat; Rook doubts it in the scene, on the wing in the rain (no office); then back to the start, as the reference long does. Labels carry dates and names.
experiments.learnings_applied: plan/learnings.json asks long-form for a shorter setup and a stronger mid-video reversal: the setup (Madrid to the crash) is 34 s of 188 s and is itself built on a reversal (twenty minutes that was not twenty minutes); the re-hook 'And nobody comes' is at 56%; a second reversal follows (the man in orange who goes away again).
experiments.rook_action: Detective action in the story world: squeezes a tuft of the insulation to test it (32; the narration says so), points it out (31), scans the ridges (41). Mannerisms: brim drops (4, 12), collar popped (9), hat off for the dead (26, 61, 65) and back on (69), coin flipped while waiting (37, 64), hat jumps when shocked (15, 51), beak tap (71), shiny rivet pocketed and hat tipped (72).
experiments.hush: two hush shots: 53 (she is carried down, before the hospital) and 60 (her face on the stretcher at the funeral)

sound_plan.first_frame: An 'impact' at 0.02 of shot 1 (the wing into the treetops), thunder at half the shot.
sound_plan.music: The score follows the segment moods: hook, tense, calm for Madrid and the apron, tense at the stairs, action for the drop, sad for the deaths (no drums), wonder for the insulation, calm for the rain, tense for the re-hook, triumph for the rescue, calm and sad for the aftermath, end.
sound_plan.effects: One or two cues a shot, each tied to something visible: rain, creaks, a gasp, an engine starting on the apron, the lurch (impact, shout), the grab of the hands, scratches for crawling and pulling fibres, a bloop for the sip, coin flips, buzzing insects, wind over the ridges, a shout from the officer, a tick as the finger lands on the list, a hit for the stamp, pops for the fireworks and the rivet.
sound_plan.voice: am_fenrir, speed 1.12; narration ducked over the bed by the engine.

source_notes: The Short's six pages (Wikipedia, NZ Herald 192 hours, Irish Examiner, View from the Wing, Mamamia, Space Coast Daily) cover the crash, her injuries, the insulation, the eight days, the officer and the carry. For the long version ten more pages were read on 20 Nov 2026 through a fetch tool that summarises pages, so no sentence is quoted and nothing is put in anyone's mouth: New York Post 2 Oct 2016 (PressReader), NZ Herald 'recounts her incredible tale', LBC, BBC News Mundo (via Prensa Libre), All That's Interesting, LADbible, two Aviation Safety Network records, Hanoi Times, and the Wikiwand copy of the Wikipedia flight article (en.wikipedia.org could not be opened in this run). Every added narrated fact is on at least two pages. Trader at a bank in Madrid: NYP, Irish Examiner. He worked for a bank in Vietnam: NYP, NZH. Thirteen years together, 'Pasje': NYP, IE, NZH, Mamamia, LBC. A romantic few days in Nha Trang: NYP, NZH, Mamamia. Claustrophobic: NYP, IE, Mamamia, BBC, LAD. He said twenty minutes: IE, Mamamia, ATI. The drop came about 50 minutes in on five pages and about 40 on one, so the narration says 'well into the flight'. He looked frightened, she said it was an air pocket, a second drop, he took her hand, black: NYP, IE, NZH, ATI, LAD. Came down too low in bad weather: Wikiwand, ASN, VFTW, LAD (no formal cause is narrated: only one page gives one). No seat belt: NYP, NZH, Mamamia, VFTW, ATI, LAD, BBC. Dead in his seat with a smile: NYP, IE, NZH (both), Mamamia, LBC. A Vietnamese businessman: NZH, Mamamia, VFTW, ATI; trousers from his suitcase: NYP, NZH, Mamamia, BBC, ATI; her skirt gone: Mamamia, ATI; told her rescuers would come: NYP, LAD, ATI; pages differ on when he died (hours, the first evening, a couple of days), so 'before long'. Stay put: NYP, NZH. Would not think of Pasje so as not to cry and weaken: NYP, NZH (both), SBS extract, BBC. A sip every two hours: IE, LBC. Rainwater all she had: NZH, Mamamia. Leeches: IE, Mamamia; insects and the smell: IE, LBC, NYP; moved away: Mamamia, LBC. O Kha mountain: Wikiwand, LAD, BBC, Hanoi Times. Felt she was dying and found it beautiful: NZH, VFTW, LBC, BBC; day six on two pages and day seven on two, so 'after nearly a week' and the label DAY 6 was removed in review. A man in orange who left: NYP, NZH, BBC (day differs; none is narrated). Men with body bags and a passenger list, she pointed to her name: NYP, NZH, BBC. Hospital in Singapore: NYP, NZH (both), VFTW (BBC as summarised says Ho Chi Minh City then the Netherlands). Family believed her dead, death notices published: Mamamia, BBC; Jaime Lupa refused to believe it: Mamamia, BBC. Funeral on a stretcher in December: NYP, NZH, Mamamia, ATI, LAD; in Breda: NYP, NZH, LAD. Compared it to a bride going down the aisle to meet her groom: NZH, ATI (paraphrased, attributed to her). Walking by New Year's Eve, back at work in February: NYP, Mamamia (IE 'within three months'). Married Jaime Lupa, children Joosje and Max, New York: NYP, IE, Mamamia. Back to the mountain in 2006: IE, NZH (both), ATI. Memoir Turbulence: all pages (published 2014 by five pages, 2016 by two; no year is narrated). Helicopter crash during the operation: Wikiwand, ASN, VFTW (seven killed), NYP and NZH (eight); the narration gives no number. Left out: the number of hip fractures, the exposed bone, the maggots, her son's diagnosis, her later divorce, any direct quotation.

quality_gate.method: One run, five review rounds. Rounds 1 to 3: low-res 16:9 contact sheets of every shot (one frame each, in three parts), then re-renders of the changed shots. Found and fixed: the scene took eight minutes to build (new objects now made straight from bmesh; about 100 s); the camera inside a tree on the second crash shot; the hands shot looking out of the open front of the cabin at empty sky (camera target given twice the set offset); the camera inside a seat on the belt shot; Willem hidden behind her and behind Rook on the apron; her back to the camera at the stairs; Rook against empty tarmac (turned so the jet is behind him); his head blocking her face in the cabin; the man who gives her the trousers embedded in the fuselage; her face hidden by her own arms and by her bowed head while brushing off insects; the move away from the wreck too dark and too far; the man in orange already turned away at the midpoint; Rook cut off by the frame when the men arrive; both hands laid across the list; her face hidden in the hospital bed; the funeral close-up upside down; a black sky above the hospital walls at night (ceiling added). Round 4: a full-length rehearsal (480x270, 6 samples, 6 fps of 3D frames, composited at 30 fps with captions, labels, overlays and sound), reviewed as two frames per shot (12% and 90%); the local gate FAILED on four static stretches (the two office shots, the aerial into Rook on the treetop, the writing desk). Fixed: stronger camera drift on 23 slow kinds, a whip into the treetop shot, one more shot in the Madrid/Vietnam segment and one in the aftermath; the same review found pictures out of step with the words in two segments (the trousers; the death notices), which were re-ordered, a label DAY 6 that the sources do not agree on (removed), and the board text clipped at the right edge (moved in). Round 5: the changed shots re-rendered, the rehearsal re-composited; the local gate PASSED; the changed shots reviewed as stills; four shots spot-checked at full resolution.
quality_gate.gate_rehearsal: 72 shots, mean 2.61 s, longest 3.84 s, first shot 2.9 s with an impact at 0.02; Rook acting in 26 of 72 shots (36%); -14.6 LUFS, peak -1.1 dBFS, voice 17.1 dB over the bed; closest match to any earlier episode 0.77 (limit 0.93). Duration 187.7 s. After the passing rehearsal only two shot weights in one segment were changed (the trousers shot runs 3.7 s instead of 3.1 s).
quality_gate.checked: Every kind in the storyboard exists in world3d.SHOTS3D or scenes.SHOTS (two flat inserts: notice_card, board); HOST lists the 23 kinds used here in which Rook is placed; no kind is used more than three times and none twice in a row; re-hook at 56%; two hush shots; labels checked against the sources; no body, blood or injury is shown beyond a bruise: the dead are a still hand, the back of a head, a man lying with his eyes closed and a closed coffin; Rook makes no joke after the hook.
quality_gate.not_met: No full-resolution, full-sample render of the whole film was made locally (the workflow does it); motion was judged at 6 fps of 3D frames. The voice and mix were measured, not listened to. The kit's human head has no eyelids, so closed eyes read as heavy-lidded. Rook's share of shots (36%) is only just over the gate's 35%. The added sources were read through a tool that summarises pages, and en.wikipedia.org could not be opened in this run (a mirror of the flight article was read instead).
